subject: Next Steps: Dedicated GPU Pool — regional parity decision & burst entitlements
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@carbona.ai>, Emily Zhou <emily.zhou@carbona.ai>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 17 May 2029 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Next Steps: Dedicated GPU Pool — regional parity decision & burst entitlements

Hi Alex / Emily —

Thanks again for the demo earlier — great alignment on the Dedicated capacity model. Per our handoff checklist, I pulled together the immediate decisions we need from your side so Ops can provision the GPU pool and we can lock the burst/autoscale knobs: 

1) Regional parity: do you need identical capacity in us-west-2 and us-east-1 at launch, or is a single-primary region with failover acceptable? Please indicate preferred primary region.
2) Burst entitlement: confirm the peak vGPU-hours/week you want available during burst windows (we suggested 10k vGPU-hours/week in the SOW draft).
3) Target go-live week (range) so we can sequence procurement and warm-burst scheduling.

Attached: carbona_sow_v1.pdf (SOW draft), carbona_burst_matrix.xlsx (example entitlement table), redwood-dedicated-checklist.md (turnup checklist).

Ops note: Sean / Kimberly — once Alex replies we will: (a) finalize instance-type mapping (A100/RTX mix), (b) reserve capacity, (c) schedule a brief cutover call for the warm-burst test.

Alex / Emily — want to set expectations: reserving regional parity increases lead time by ~7–10 business days compared to single region. If cost sensitivity is a factor, we can propose asymmetric parity (higher capacity in primary, smaller hot-standby).

Next steps: please reply with the three items above and any procurement timing constraints.

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
m: +1 (415) 555-0192
[attachment: carbona_sow_v1.pdf (pdf)] [attachment: carbona_burst_matrix.xlsx (xlsx)] [attachment: redwood-dedicated-checklist.md (text)]

From: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@carbona.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Emily Zhou <emily.zhou@carbona.ai>, Procurement <procurement@carbona.ai>
Date: Fri, 17 May 2029 11:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Next Steps: Dedicated GPU Pool — regional parity decision & burst entitlements

Monica —

Thanks, this is helpful. Quick answers from our side: 

- Regional parity: we'd like primary in us-west-2 and a smaller hot-standby in us-east-1 (80/20 split) so latency-sensitive traffic stays local but we have failover capacity.
- Burst entitlement: can you scope the 10k vGPU-hours/week into a sample breakdown by job class? We'll attach our internal expected job mix later today.
- Go-live: target week of Jun 24th. Procurement needs the SOW and an estimate for invoices by Jun 3rd.

Two questions for Ops: does Redwood support mixing A100 and H100 instances in the same pool and apply autoscale policies across them, or should we map jobs to homogeneous sub-pools? Also, what's the warm-burst test duration you recommend?

Emily / Procurement — looping you in for timelines and SOW review.

—Alex
Alex Rivera
Head of ML Platform, Carbona
alex.rivera@carbona.ai
[attachment: carbona_internal_job_mix.csv (csv)]

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@carbona.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 17 May 2029 14:06:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Next Steps: Dedicated GPU Pool — regional parity decision & burst entitlements

Alex — thanks for the quick reply and the 80/20 direction. A few technical clarifications from Ops to make sure provisioning matches expectations: 

- Mixed-instance pools: we recommend mapping at the job-class level to homogeneous sub-pools for predictable latency (e.g., an A100 sub-pool for high-throughput embeddings, an H100 sub-pool for large-context generation). Redwood can route by job labels so the platform appears unified; autoscale policies apply per sub-pool.
- Warm-burst test: we suggest a staged ramp: 0% -> 50% -> 100% over a 2-hour window with synthetic traffic, followed by a 1-hour soak. That surfaces autoscale policy issues and cache warmup.
- Instance types & quotas: for us-west-2 we can reserve A100-80GB and H100-80GB; lead time for H100 is currently ~9 business days.

Recommended sample config (high-level):
- Primary (us-west-2): 320 vGPUs (A100 80GB x 160 + H100 80GB x 40)
- Hot-standby (us-east-1): 80 vGPUs (A100 80GB x 20)
- Burst window entitlement: provisioned base 200 vGPUs with burst to 400 vGPUs for up to 24 hours (capped by the weekly vGPU-hours entitlement).

I'll have the formal provisioning ticket and reservation ETA after procurement confirms the SOW.

—Sean
Sean Gallagher
Senior Technical Program Manager, Capacity & Ops
Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@carbona.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Procurement <procurement@carbona.ai>
Date: Sun, 19 May 2029 09:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Next Steps: Dedicated GPU Pool — regional parity decision & burst entitlements

Alex / Procurement team —

Following Sean's recommendations, we've updated the entitlement matrix and the checklist attached. Action items for Carbona to unblock reservations: 

- Sign SOW (we'll accept redlines; legal expects comments by May 27th to keep the Jun 3rd invoice target).
- Confirm final weekly vGPU-hours cap (we used 10k as a working number; please update the attached sheet).
- Provide network egress constraints (if any) and IP allowlist for the private endpoints.

We've set a provisional go-live week of Jun 24th in the calendar; Monica will send the invite for the warm-burst dry run (2.5 hours). Attached: carbona_burst_matrix.xlsx (updated), redwood-dedicated-checklist.md (with Ops staging steps).

Kimberly Park

Monica — please put a 30-minute kickoff on Jun 4th to walk through the warm-burst plan and reservation timeline; Emily will join.

Appreciate the fast turnaround.

—Alex
